sections.overview: Porcellio scaber is a familiar European woodlouse that has spread widely beyond its native range.
sections.identification: Its body is rough and strongly tuberculate, with variable colouration. Unlike P. spinicornis, its mottling is irregular rather than forming a yellow-flanked stripe. Its telson is less rounded than that of P. dilatatus.
sections.habitat: It uses many habitats, especially under stones, dead wood and leaf litter, and tolerates drier sites than Oniscus asellus.
sections.diet: It feeds on decaying organic matter, including leaf litter, fungi and animal remains.
sections.behavior: It often shelters in damp refuges but can also climb walls and enter buildings.
sections.reproduction: Females carry eggs and hatchlings in a fluid-filled brood pouch.
sections.ecology: Experiments have documented viable seed dispersal after it eats fruits.
sections.conservation: The British group lists it as Least Concern in Great Britain; this regional status is not a global assessment.
